Bringing the shape of incoming work into dock assignments.

Role
MBA Pathways Operations Manager Intern
Period
2026
Focus
Inbound operations & load balancing

The operational problem

Inbound placement decisions needed to account for the work arriving in each trailer and where that work needed to go. Package-mix and destination information could help make the load-balancing implications of a placement decision easier to understand.

The opportunity was to bring those inputs into a practical decision aid for inbound operations.

My contribution

During my Amazon operations internship, I developed a trailer dock-assignment platform using package-mix and destination data to recommend trailer placement. The work connected an operational problem to a tool designed around a specific decision.

The platform’s output was a placement recommendation. This case focuses on that decision-support role and my contribution to bringing the relevant inputs together.

Making the workflow discussable

To make the general decision process available for public exploration, I separately rebuilt it as Dockflow. That independent portfolio simulator uses newly written code, fictional trailers, and synthetic facility data.

A reviewer can explore prioritization, compatible door recommendations, and simulated operator decisions without accessing Amazon systems or data. It provides something concrete to discuss alongside the workplace experience.

Keeping the two projects distinct

Dockflow has its own verification record. Simulated approval, undo, and local decision history are features of the portfolio rebuild and should not be attributed to the original workplace tool. Its simulated results do not establish workplace business impact.

The original experience explains the operational problem and my contribution. The public demonstration makes the general constraints visible and lets a visitor explore how a recommendation changes as the fictional operating state changes.
